managedRouting.description: Rules run in order at each node. Both nodes must be included in your current purchase.
managedRouting.templateDescription: Choose destination matchers for member routes. Categories combine with AND; entries within each category combine with OR. Empty categories match all traffic. Domain rules support full:, domain:, keyword:, regexp: and geosite: selectors.
managedRouting.graphHint: The graph fits automatically. Select a node or template with Enter or Space; scroll the page normally.
managedRouting.empty: No custom routes. Traffic follows the node's default routing.
managedRouting.disabled: These routes need review after an access, template or endpoint change. Review and save to apply them again.
managedRouting.saveFailed: The routes could not be saved. Check your node access and templates, then retry.

errors.routing_endpoint_unavailable: A selected host is unavailable or does not belong to the selected node and your current access. Choose an authorized host.
errors.routing_context_unproven: These routes require fixed destination metadata and direct fallbacks. Ask an administrator to review sniffing, client mappings and proxy chains.
errors.routing_loop: These conditions create a routing loop. Change the destination or matchers.
errors.routing_overlap_unproven: The matcher overlap could not be proven safe. Use more specific domain, IP or port conditions.
errors.routing_analysis_limit: This graph exceeds the safety analysis limit. Simplify its rules or selectors.
errors.routing_invalid_rule: Each rule needs a unique ID and two different accessible nodes.

managedRouting.templateDetailsHint: Match categories combine with AND; entries in each category combine with OR.
managedRouting.treeHint: Select a node to edit routes, or a template to view its match settings.

routeSpeedtest.resultsHint: The test continues if you close this window. Reopen it to view progress and results.
routeSpeedtest.metered: Uses your traffic quota. Each pair: up to 32 MiB down, 8 MiB up, 60 seconds.
routeSpeedtest.requirements: Save and trace an active route before testing. Nodes must be synchronized.
routeSpeedtest.failed: The route test could not start. Your route draft is retained.
routeSpeedtest.uncertain: Completed pairs are retained. Traffic-consuming commands will not repeat automatically.
